Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.hebrew: כל דמים: החיצונים שנכנסו להיכל לכפר — פסולין. ואף על גב דלא כתיב אלא 'וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה וגו'', מרבה רבי עקיבא קדשי קדשים וקדשים קלים מריבויא ד'כל' ו'כל' לקמן ב'כל הזבחים שנתערבו' (זבחים דף פב.):
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.english: All blood: This is referring to the external blood that entered the Sanctuary to atone, which is disqualified. This is so even though the verse only states: “And any sin offering, any of whose blood is brought, etc.” Rabbi Akiva includes Most Holy Offerings and Lesser Holy Offerings by expounding the superfluous words “kol” and “kol” (all) in the verse cited later in the chapter “In all mixed offerings” (Zevachim 82a).

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:13:1.hebrew: קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם - במנחה הוא דכתיב וקא אמר רבי שמעון: מדקא מקיש מנחות לחטאת ואשם, להכי מקיש [לשניהם], לומר לך: דיש מהם כחטאת, ויש מהם כאשם, שתהא מנחת חוטא כחטאת דלא לשמה פסולה, ומנחת נדבה כאשם דכשר שלא לשמו.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:1.hebrew: ולרבנן - דפליגי עליה דרבי אליעזר במתניתין, למאי הלכתא וכו'?

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:2.hebrew: חטאת כתיב בה (ויקרא ד׳:כ״ד): וסמך ידו על ראש החטאת.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:20:1.hebrew: אמרו דבר אחד: that Rabbi Eliezer also disqualifies other offerings slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering at its designated time, or for the sake of a ḥatat offering all year round, and Rabbi Yoḥanan derives this from a baraita below.

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:13:1.english: A sinner's meal offering is like a sin offering - This is not a derivation from one to the other. For even though we derive from peace offerings that a sin offering is a *mitzva* (to be brought for its sake) as stated above, its indispensability is written explicitly. And a voluntary meal offering is like a guilt offering not because it is derived from a guilt offering for the *mitzva* (to be brought for its sake), since the meal offering itself is juxtaposed with peace offerings like a guilt offering, but rather to say that it is not like a sin offering.

Zevachim 11a:12.english: The Gemara resumes its discussion of the dispute in the mishna between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis. Granted, according to the Rabbis, who say that a guilt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake is fit, that is why a meal offering is juxtaposed with a sin offering, and a meal offering is also juxtaposed with a guilt offering.

Zevachim 11a:17.english: The Gemara asks: And as for Rabbi Shimon, does he expound this verse for this purpose and expound it for that purpose, deriving two different *halakhot* from a single verse?

Zevachim 11a:20.english: The mishna teaches: Yosef ben Ḥoni says: Other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering or a ḥatat offering are unfit. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Yosef ben Ḥoni and Rabbi Eliezer said the same thing, i.e., Rabbi Eliezer agrees with Yosef ben Ḥoni.
